conventions.convention: Filling coefficient p/q means attached meridian pμ+qλ; simultaneous sign change preserves the unoriented slope, and the meridional slope is 1/0.

The surgery triad uses primitive representatives with all three cyclic consecutive determinants equal to +1. Trajectories use orientation dt∧or(Y) and the negative gradient equation for the perturbed Chern–Simons functional.
The representation, Property P, meridian-detection and complement statements assume full AC. The instanton data definition asserts no analytic existence, exact triangle or rank theorem.
Trefoil generators are positive meridians with common upper-collar basing paths. In the rightward-overstrand chart, m_R=m_o m_L m_o⁻¹; the crossing triples are (b,c,a), (c,a,b), (a,b,c).

Meridian detection and extension of the particular exterior homeomorphism are asserted for nontrivial knots. For two unknots, ambient equivalence is asserted without meridian preservation by that particular homeomorphism.
The longitude-twist matrix acts on column coordinates in the ordered basis (μ,λ), with μ the disk-boundary meridian and λ the product-circle longitude.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a nontrivial smooth knot K⊂S³ and coprime integers p,q with |p|=1 and q≠0, π₁(E_K(p/q)) admits a homomorphism to SU(2) with noncyclic image.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a nontrivial smooth knot K⊂S³ and coprime integers p,q with q≠0, π₁(E_K(p/q)) is nontrivial.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a nontrivial smooth knot K⊂S³ and coprime integers p,q not both zero, E_K(p/q) is homeomorphic to S³ if and only if q=0, in which case p=±1.
The specified based trefoil group has presentation ⟨a,b | aba=bab⟩. Its abelianization is isomorphic to Z, but the group is nonabelian.

published_dependencies.used_for: Nonzero first homology implies nontrivial fundamental group in the Property P homology cases; its path-connectedness hypothesis is established locally.
Comparison of normalized tubular-neighbourhood germs in the unknot branch of the complement theorem, retaining the matching normal-identification and countable-choice hypotheses.
The cited solid-torus extension supplier extends disk-face maps and the cut-open ball map radially.
Smooth knot, orientation-preserving ambient-isotopy and unoriented-equivalence conventions.
Based loop classes and first-loop-first concatenation in the group computations and counterexample.
Loop concatenation, inverses and induced group isomorphisms under complement homeomorphisms.
Full AC assumptions and their implication of countable choice.

concerns.concern: The Example says the displayed rectangle has 'opposite sides ... identified' and that its diagonal ending at (2,1) represents 2μ+λ. The TikZ rectangle is [0,2]×[0,1]. Identifying its opposite sides gives horizontal period 2, so that diagonal represents μ+λ in the rectangle's fundamental-cycle basis. It represents 2μ+λ only with horizontal period 1, requiring the additional unit-lattice identifications. The explicit extension and matrix calculation are sound; the diagram's stated quotient convention is inconsistent.

The title says 'Admissible instanton surgery-triangle data', whereas the Definition expressly defines candidate data with arbitrary principal SO(3) bundles and supplies no bundle admissibility condition. The title should agree with the deliberately qualified candidate-data interface.

seams_checked.note: The supplier theorem and local conjugacy lemma match the trefoil's positive-meridian assignment and crossing equations. The crossing-free unknot case is included. No reverse dependency is asserted.

Chosen compact exteriors, meridians and preferred longitudes agree. The exterior-homology supplier gives the meridian generator and longitude kernel under countable choice; the owned consumers assume full AC.
The pμ+qλ convention and homology formula agree, including p=0 and q=0. Owned proofs establish connectedness and supply countable choice from full AC.

The actual logical use is the nontrivial-exterior boundary-incompressibility lemma, whose smooth-disk conclusion matches the complement proof. No Khovanov detector or singular-instanton rank theorem is claimed to prove Property P.

The meridian-preserving extension supplier covers the actual boundary homeomorphism, carries core to core and preserves its orientation sign. No hyperbolicity assumption is imported. The example's explicit extension is correct independently of its diagram concern.
